title: 2021 Fall AMC 10B Problem 17
statement: Distinct lines \(\ell\) and \(m\) lie in the \(xy\)-plane. They intersect at the origin. Point \(P(-1, 4)\) is reflected about line \(\ell\) to point \(P',\) and then \(P'\) is reflected about line \(m\) to point \(P''.\) The equation of line \(\ell\) is \(5x - y = 0,\) and the coordinates of \(P''\) are \((4,1).\) What is the equation of line \(m?\)

solutions.text:
Two reflections across lines through the origin are equivalent to a rotation by twice the angle from the first reflecting line to the second.

The point \((-1,4)\) is sent to \((4,1),\) which is a \(90^\circ\) clockwise rotation. Therefore line \(m\) is \(45^\circ\) clockwise from line \(\ell.\)

The slope of \(\ell\) is \(5.\) If \(\theta_m=\theta_\ell-45^\circ,\) then \[\tan\theta_m=\frac{5-1}{1+5}=\frac23.\]

Thus line \(m\) is \(y=\frac23x,\) or \(2x-3y=0.\)

Thus, the answer is D .
hints: Two reflections through intersecting lines equal a rotation
Compare the angle change from \((-1,4)\) to \((4,1)\)
